opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Miller (employee ID E017) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E017.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jennifer Miller (Analyst, full_time) requests write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write (admin only if their role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security check: Jennifer Miller (E017) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; write is not permitted with basic training. Requested write exceeds the maximum allowed, so recommend read.
reason: Jennifer Miller (E017) requests write access to Source Code. The notes conflict on employment type: the HR note says full_time and recommends write, while the Security note identifies her as a contractor with basic security training and recommends read. Under the contractor policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; basic training does not permit write, so the maximum allowed is read. Because the requested write exceeds the maximum under the security-verified facts, I grant the maximum: read.
